question: How does the World Health Organization define an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Any termination performed exclusively in a tertiary hospital setting
options.B: A procedure carried out by persons lacking skills or in an environment below minimal medical standards
options.C: A spontaneous miscarriage occurring during the first trimester of pregnancy
options.D: A legal termination performed after twenty weeks of gestation

explanation: An unsafe abortion is officially defined as a termination procedure carried out either by persons lacking the necessary skills or in an environment that does not conform to minimal medical standards, or both. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h1)

question: Which demographic group in Nigeria is disproportionately affected by unsafe abortion due to limited access to services?

options.C: Young women, adolescents, and rural dwellers
options.D: Male children under the age of five

explanation: Young women, adolescents, and rural dwellers are disproportionately affected because they often lack access to comprehensive reproductive health education and modern contraceptive services. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h1)

question: Under Nigerian criminal law, when is abortion legally permitted?

options.A: Whenever the pregnant woman requests it
options.B: Only when the mother's life is in direct danger
options.C: In cases of minor financial hardship
options.D: During the first trimester for any reason

explanation: Nigerian law restricts abortion strictly to circumstances where the continuation of the pregnancy places the mother's life in direct danger. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h2)

question: What is a major clinical consequence of the social stigma and restrictive laws surrounding abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: Patients immediately report providers to the police
options.B: Women delay seeking professional medical care for complications
options.C: Contraceptives become completely free in all pharmacies
options.D: Maternal mortality rates drop to zero

explanation: Due to fear of judgment, stigma, and legal repercussions, women frequently delay seeking professional medical care when experiencing complications from unsafe abortions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h2)

question: What is a primary clinical sign of hypovolemic shock resulting from severe hemorrhage after an unsafe abortion?

options.D: Normal pulse and elevated blood pressure

explanation: Hypovolemic shock from severe blood loss typically presents with an elevated heart rate (tachycardia) and a drop in blood pressure (hypotension). [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h3)

question: What immediate nursing intervention is critical for a patient presenting with septic shock due to an incomplete unsafe abortion?

options.A: Administering oral vitamins and scheduling a follow-up in six months
options.B: Establishing large-bore IV access and administering broad-spectrum IV antibiotics
options.C: Discharging the patient immediately with strict bed rest instructions
options.D: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to stimulate uterine contractions

explanation: Stabilization requires urgent establishment of large-spectrum IV access for resuscitation and administration of broad-spectrum IV antibiotics to combat spreading infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h3)

question: What is a common long-term reproductive consequence of ascending pelvic infections following an unsafe abortion?

options.B: Tubal occlusion, chronic PID, and secondary infertility
options.C: Permanent cessation of all hormonal activity
options.D: Complete immunity to sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Ascending infections often cause severe pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), leading to tubal occlusion, scarring, and secondary infertility. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h4)

question: What condition involving intrauterine adhesions and scarring can result from aggressive instrumental evacuation of the uterus?
explanation: Asherman's syndrome is characterized by intrauterine adhesions and scar tissue formation resulting from trauma to the endometrial lining during uterine evacuation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h4)

question: Which psychological conditions are frequently observed among patients who have survived an unsafe abortion?

options.B: Depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD)

explanation: The trauma, fear, and stigma associated with unsafe abortion often trigger depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder in affected patients. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h5)

question: How can nursing staff best mitigate the social and psychological distress experienced by abortion care patients?

options.A: By publicly scolding patients to discourage future occurrences
options.B: By providing compassionate, non-judgmental support and maintaining confidentiality
options.C: By ignoring psychological symptoms and focusing solely on vital signs
options.D: By reporting all patients immediately to local religious leaders

explanation: Offering compassionate, non-judgmental care and strict confidentiality helps patients feel safe and supports their psychological recovery. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h5)

question: What physical assessment findings should immediately raise a nurse's suspicion of a septic or unsafe abortion?

options.A: Normal blood pressure and slow, regular pulse
options.B: Lower abdominal pain, fever, and foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.C: Weight gain and bilateral peripheral edema
options.D: Clear, odorless vaginal discharge and normal temperature

explanation: Lower abdominal pain, fever, and foul-smelling discharge are classic clinical indicators of infection and uterine sepsis following an unsafe abortion. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h6)

question: Why is it important for nurses to identify social and demographic risk factors for unsafe abortion?

options.A: To report patients to law enforcement agencies
options.B: To identify vulnerable individuals early and anticipate potential complications
options.C: To deny care to individuals who break cultural laws
options.D: To determine the exact financial cost of the hospital stay

explanation: Recognizing risk factors allows nurses to identify vulnerable patients early, facilitating rapid triage and anticipation of life-threatening complications. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h6)

question: What are the three core components of Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: Surgery, financial auditing, and legal prosecution
options.B: Emergency treatment, contraceptive counseling, and linkage to reproductive health services
options.C: Mandatory isolation, religious counseling, and long-term bed rest
options.D: Routine blood transfusions, herbal therapy, and immediate discharge

explanation: PAC comprises emergency treatment of complications, contraceptive counseling and provision, and linkage to broader reproductive healthcare services. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h7)

question: When should contraceptive counseling and service provision occur within the framework of Post-Abortion Care?

options.A: Only after the patient experiences a second unsafe abortion
options.B: Before patient discharge, while still in the healthcare facility
options.C: Six months after the initial hospital visit during a routine check-up
options.D: Never, as it is outside the scope of nursing practice

explanation: Providing contraceptive counseling and services before discharge ensures the patient is protected against another unintended pregnancy before leaving the facility. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h7)

question: What is a primary preventative measure nurses can implement to reduce the incidence of unsafe abortions?

options.A: Restricting public access to family planning information
options.B: Promoting comprehensive sex education and expanding access to modern contraception
options.C: Encouraging early marriage and large family sizes
options.D: Eliminating all obstetric and gynecological services

explanation: Promoting sex education and expanding access to modern contraception addresses the root cause of unsafe abortion by preventing unintended pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h8)

question: How do youth-friendly health services established by nurses contribute to reproductive health?

options.A: By providing a welcoming, non-judgmental environment for adolescents seeking guidance
options.B: By reporting all sexually active youths to local authorities
options.C: By restricting healthcare access strictly to married individuals
options.D: By focusing exclusively on geriatric care needs

explanation: Youth-friendly health services offer a welcoming, non-judgmental space where adolescents can safely access education, counseling, and contraceptive services. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h8)
